caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Public debt has swung violently with the peso rather than with borrowing alone. It fell from 70.8% of GDP in 2006 to 38.9% in 2011, then rose steadily: 44.7% in 2014, 53.1% in 2016, and 85.2% in 2018 when devaluation revalued foreign-currency debt and the $57bn IMF Stand-By Arrangement (the largest in IMF history, $44bn disbursed) added new obligations. It hit 103.8% in 2020 on COVID plus further devaluation, then 154.6% in 2023 - a year-end artifact of the mega-devaluation inflating the dollar value of peso debt - before normalizing to 84.7% in 2024 and a projected 80.3% in 2025. Argentina restructured ~$65bn in foreign-law bonds in 2020, refinanced the IMF exposure with a $44bn Extended Fund Facility in 2022, and secured a fresh $20bn EFF in April 2025 ($12bn disbursed upfront) to back Milei's stabilization. Sustainability hinges entirely on maintaining the fiscal surplus, since the debt stock is heavily dollar-linked.
inflation_management: Argentina's inflation record is the region's most extreme: double-digit inflation in every measured year and no monetary regime that held for long. Inflation ran 6.3-10.9% through 2006-2013 (official figures for that era are widely regarded as understated), then 25.7% in 2017, 34.3% in 2018, and 53.5% in 2019 as the peso collapsed under the 2018 crisis. It stayed near 42-48% in 2020-2021, accelerated to 72.4% in 2022 and 133.5% in 2023 as fiscal dominance and money printing intensified, and peaked at 219.9% in 2024 after Javier Milei's December 2023 ~55% mega-devaluation passed through prices. The data contain no inflation values for 2014-2016. Disinflation in 2024-25 came from a fiscal shock (spending cuts worth roughly 5% of GDP), a tight crawling peg, and a new FX band of 1,000-1,400 pesos per dollar introduced in April 2025; the IMF projects 41.9% inflation for 2025.

key_events.event: Global financial crisis; Argentina rode out the shock but doubled down on state intervention, including the 2012 YPF expropriation.
Technical default on restructured bonds after US courts sided with holdout 'vulture fund' creditors.
Peso crisis: capital flight forced the Macri government to take a record $57bn IMF Stand-By Arrangement; recession and 34.3% inflation followed.
Peronist Alberto Fernandez won the presidency; debt restructuring talks began.
COVID-19 contraction; Argentina restructured ~$65bn of foreign-law bonds and suspended the 2018 IMF program.
New $44bn IMF Extended Fund Facility to refinance the 2018 exposure; inflation crossed 70%.
Libertarian outsider Javier Milei won the November election, then devalued the peso ~55% in December; inflation hit 133.5%.
IMF approved a $20bn EFF in April 2025 with a 1,000-1,400 peso FX band; inflation projected down to 41.9%.

outlook_next_decade: The near term is unusually promising by Argentine standards - fiscal surplus, rapid disinflation, and restored market access - but the entire edifice rests on sustained political support for austerity and on accumulating reserves inside the new FX band. Upside is real: Vaca Muerta energy, lithium, and the large-investment incentive regime have drawn ~$30bn in announced projects. The risks are equally Argentine: a history of 22 derailed IMF programs, dollar-denominated debt that punishes any devaluation, and a political cycle that has reversed every stabilization since the 1990s. Expect volatility, not a straight line.
